title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: These are to inform you that we got safe home. That evening after we left you a little after ten o'clock and got but three shad. I felt but poorly for several days after I got home, and now I have got better which I am thankful for. we found little Tommy very poorly, and now he has got better. & it has so fell out that Enoch has not been to Philadelphia since we saw you. He has been poorly some part of the time, but he is now gone to Burlington. And if things fall out according to expectation, I believe he will be at Philadelphia next-third day and I should be very glad to hear how brother Thornton is and whether he has set sail for England or not. And if I cannot see you I should be glad for to hear from you.

postscript.p: No more at this time but my kind love to you all
